subject: Sales discovery: model fit & quality regression concern
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Rogers <emma@acme.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + model recommendations (Acme)

Thanks again for the time this morning, Emma - great to learn more about Acme.ai's customer support summarization flow and the latency/cost targets you mentioned. Quick recap and next steps: 

- Problem summary: you need a model that maintains high extractive fidelity on long support threads (avg ~1.2k tokens) while keeping 95th percentile latency under 600ms and unit cost predictable.
- Our recommendation (prototype): redwood-open-3.1.0 (quantized) for summary generation + reranker stage with redwood-rerank-1.0 for final filtering. See attached recommendations and benchmark summary.
- Benchmarks: we ran your sample prompt set (50 conversations) and observed a ~6% improvement in ROUGE-1 vs the baseline you shared, with 20% lower per-token cost after KV-prefix caching. Full CSV attached.
- Prompt sets & evals: linked Drive has the prompt set and eval harness (precision/recall slices by intent). Please confirm the priority metric (precision @ top-3? F1?) so we can tune the scoring thresholds.

Action items / next steps:
1) Can you upload a broader sample (200-500 conversations) or point us to an S3/Drive folder we can pull from?
2) We can pin a stable model variant for your account while we run a larger regression analysis. Let us know if you want immediate pinning.
3) I'll loop in our infra team if you report any regression after model updates - we have a rollback/pinning playbook.

Attachments: redwood_model_recommendation.pdf (PDF, 120KB), acme_benchmark_results.csv (CSV, 24KB)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
https://www.redwood.com

From: Emma Rogers <emma@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + model recommendations (Acme)

Hi Marissa - thanks for the quick recap and the recommendations. Overall this aligns with what we discussed. A couple of items from our side: 

- We ran the recommended config against last week's production snapshot and observed a regression on extractive entity fidelity for the "billing dispute" intent. I'm attaching a small diff (10 examples) showing before/after outputs where the new variant omits key invoice references.
- This is impacting a small but high-value slice of customers - we can share more examples if it helps triage.
- Question: did Redwood push a model variant update on Saturday? The timing matches the day we started seeing the change. If so, would you be able to pin us to the prior variant while you investigate? We need to avoid the regression hitting the rest of our corpus.

Attachment: acme_output_diffs.zip (ZIP, 2.1MB)

Also, Procurement asked for an updated SOW and timeline once we confirm pin/rollback approach.

Emma Rogers
Head of ML Ops | Acme.ai
emma@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap + model recommendations (Acme) -- regression concern

Forwarding Acme's note and diffs - they reported a regression in the "billing dispute" intent after what looks like a recent model variant push. Can you triage? Questions:
- Can we pin Acme to the previous variant immediately?
- If pinning isn't feasible, what's the fastest rollback path?
- ETA for a root-cause diff run (we should do token-level and prompt-normalized diffs).

I've attached their diffs and our benchmark CSV. Please reply with recommended remediation steps and a timeline I can share with the customer.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap + model recommendations (Acme) -- regression concern

Thanks for flagging this, Marissa. Quick summary of proposed remediation: 

1) Immediate mitigation: we can pin Acme.ai to model variant redwood-open-3.1.0-20260827 (the snapshot prior to last weekend's rollout) for their account only. Pinning is a config change and can be applied within ~4 hours after approval.

2) Investigation plan: run a diff job across their provided sample (and an expanded sample if they can provide it). We'll run both prompt-normalized diffs and token-level scoring (log-perplexity and entity recall) to isolate whether the change is from tokenizer/quantization or a model weight delta. ETA: full diff for a 500-example set in ~48 hours (compute/time dependent).

3) Rollback: if we identify a clear degradation caused by the recent variant, ops can roll back the global variant for a limited period while we patch. That is higher-friction (coordination + infra), but feasible within 24 hours if urgent.

4) Communication: I'll prepare a short summary doc with failing examples and suggested mitigations (pin + patch timeline). I'll include a trace id for the diff job and link the run to the customer's HubSpot deal.

Related links: internal runbook: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/model-pinning
Trace ID (proposed): rwd-diff-20260902-acme-17

If Marissa gets go-ahead from Acme to pin, we'll schedule the config change and confirm when it's live.

--Dylan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Rogers <emma@acme.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + model recommendations (Acme) - next steps and timeline

Emma - thanks for the examples, and for flagging the customer-impact slice. Here's the immediate plan from Redwood: 

1) Pin: With your approval we will pin Acme.ai to redwood-open-3.1.0-20260827 (account-scoped) to prevent additional regressions. Dylan estimates this can be applied within ~4 hours of your confirmation.
2) Diff & analysis: Dylan's team will run the diff job across the attached examples + an expanded set if you can provide it. ETA for a full report ~48 hours (rwd-diff-20260902-acme-17).
3) Rollback (if needed): If the diff shows a clear quality regression tied to last weekend's rollout, ops can roll back the global variant within 24 hours; we would coordinate timing with you.

Action items for Acme: please reply to confirm "PIN NOW" if you want us to apply the account pin immediately. Also, if you can drop a 200-example anonymized sample to the Drive link below, it will speed up the analysis.
